sentence: A model that reads a viewer's liked films in order and scores the next film (Kang and McAuley, 2018). This project’s public title is Next-Movie Recommender: Rating-aware Self-Attention.
A score that is 1 when the hidden film is in position 1, smaller when it is lower in the top 10, and 0 when it is missing.
The share of viewers whose hidden film appears anywhere in the top 10.
Hide each viewer's last liked film, then ask the method to guess it.
A rule that position t may look only at positions up to t, so the model cannot see the answer it is predicting.
A learned list of numbers that stands for one film.
A training penalty that is larger when the model is confidently wrong.
A viewer whose history is empty, or contains only films this catalog does not know.
The share of films that appear in at least one viewer's top 10.
Response-time marks. p95 means 95% of requests finished in this time or less.
The hidden film is ranked against every film the viewer has not already seen, not against a random sample of wrong films.
The HTTP menu other programs use to ask for five films.
The model learned information that would not have been available at the moment of the prediction.
